_comment: Six archetypes; for each — 3-5 visual variants of distinct individuals of that archetype. Each variant is one image-model-friendly noun phrase in English. The generator picks one variant per banner so all three images for the same archetype show DIFFERENT merchants of the same archetype.
IVAN_DURAK: young flaxen-haired peasant lad with smiling face and a slight foolish grin, wearing white linen rubakha embroidered with red cross-stitch, simple kushak belt, bast-shoe lapti
freckled red-haired barefoot wanderer in patched grey kaftan and birch-bark hat, carrying a small wooden staff and a kerchief-bundle on a stick over his shoulder
dreamy chestnut-haired youth lying back on the warm side of a clay stove, in a striped homespun shirt, cheeks pink, blue eyes gazing up at the ceiling, sleepy and untroubled
stocky black-bearded young muzhik in a sheepskin tulup and felt valenki, wide guileless face, sitting astride a grey wolf in deep snow
lanky sandy-haired youth in a crooked papakha and a too-big embroidered coat, balancing a bundle of magic feathers under one arm, expression naively pleased
BABA_YAGA: ancient hunchbacked crone with a long crooked nose hooking down to her chin, wild grey hair under a black headscarf with white skull pattern, tattered dark sarafan, holding a bony pestle, eyes glowing pale yellow
skeletal forest witch in a ragged dark green cloak of moss and pine needles, hair like spider-web, a black raven perched on her bony shoulder, knobbed walking stick in her gnarled hand

stout broad-shouldered hag with iron-grey braids and a single red eye, wearing a crimson and black sarafan stitched with bone beads, stirring a great copper cauldron, mushrooms sprouting from her shawl
tall gaunt witch in a black fur-trimmed dushegreya and tall pointed kokoshnik woven from chicken bones, holding a broom of dry birch twigs, fingernails long and yellow
ancient toothless granny crouched on the stove ledge of her hut on chicken legs, wrapped in many shawls of black and rust-red, clutching a small wooden bowl, single tooth showing
ZOLUSHKA: soot-dusted young woman with chestnut hair tied in a simple braid, wearing a patched grey homespun sarafan and a coarse linen apron, kind tired blue eyes, smooth clear face, holding a wooden broom, no scars no wounds

barefoot raven-haired girl in a sky-blue sarafan that is starting to glow at the hem with silver threads, glass slipper just appearing in her hand, twilight light around her, smooth unblemished complexion
fair-haired stepdaughter in white linen sorochka and dark patched sarafan, hand-feeding doves from a wooden trencher in a frosty courtyard, expression gentle and resolute, smooth clear skin no scars
young woman with golden hair under a simple white kerchief, sitting at a low stool sorting heaps of buckwheat and millet by the firelight, mice gathered to help her, smooth clear complexion no scars

girl half-transformed: torn working dress on one side, shimmering pearl-embroidered sarafan and silver kokoshnik on the other, fairy-godmother light pouring over her shoulder, smooth clear face no scars
KOSCHEI: tall gaunt sorcerer with skeletal frame, deathly pale skin stretched over high cheekbones, sunken green eyes, long black robe with iron-bone clasps, crowned with a thin twisted iron diadem, fingers tipped with black nails
ancient lich-king seated on a throne of intertwined bones and rusty swords, draped in a moth-eaten purple velvet mantle, holding a small black egg in his clawed hand
shadow-thin warlock in a long fur-trimmed cloak of crow feathers, half-skeletal face partly hidden behind a high collar, riding a gaunt black horse through fog
decrepit immortal with a wispy grey beard down to his chest, dressed in tarnished silver armour over black chainmail, leaning on a staff topped with a chained skull
lean noble with bone-white braided hair, in a high-collared black brocade kaftan stitched with silver runes, behind him a chained iron chest in a treasury of skulls
TSAR_GOROKH: rotund elderly tsar with a vast white beard cascading over a green and gold brocade kaftan, tall fur-trimmed shapka Monomakha crown studded with rubies, holding a curled sceptre, fond chuckle on his ruddy face
stout old king with thin grey hair and a forked beard, dressed in a heavy crimson and ermine mantle, sitting on a throne shaped like a giant pea pod, plump hands resting on his round belly
jolly bald monarch with curly white sideburns, jewel-encrusted golden crown perched askew, wearing a mustard-yellow kaftan embroidered with green peas and pearls, drinking sweet kvass from a horn cup
stately silver-bearded tsar with sad benevolent eyes, in a blue and gold robe, holding a tall staff with a globe of carved peas, a flock of carved wooden pigeons at his feet
rumpled folk-tale king in slippers and a long nightcap with a tassel, brocade kaftan unbuttoned at the chest, surrounded by piles of scattered gold coins and ledgers
KOLOBOK: round golden-baked bread roll with a smooth crust, two cheerful black-bead eyes and a wide cracked-crust grin, small flour-dusted limbs, rolling along a forest path, late autumn leaves around
plump dough-roll character with rosy buttery cheeks, an embroidered red sash tied around its middle, tiny stick-thin arms holding a kerchief-bundle, smug expression
weather-worn dark-baked roll with raisin eyes and a slightly burnt crust, sitting on a windowsill of a peasant izba, pretending to look innocent
round shiny brioche-like character with a curled crust on top like a topknot, holding a small painted spoon, bouncing along a country lane in front of a forest
fat sourdough roll with poppy-seed freckles, a wide grin showing crumb-teeth, leaning back lazily on a hay bale in a sunlit field
